content: The test image shows a macro close-up of a plant stem covered in dense gray-brown fuzzy sporulation (conidiophores with conidia), with a dark black sclerotium-like structure visible in the upper right. This strongly suggests Gray Mold (Botrytis cinerea) or possibly Sclerotinia. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference Gray Mold image shows late-stage brown collapsed tissue, while the test image is a macro close-up showing active sporulation. The dense gray-brown fuzzy conidiophores on the stem and the black sclerotium visible in the upper right corner are classic features of Botrytis cinerea (Gray Mold). Botrytis forms black sclerotia and produces characteristic stalked conidiophores exactly as seen in the test image.
